name: Concept Country - Gradient-Free Weight Editing Reduces Overthinking in Qwen3.8-27B (working paper v1)
notes: Working paper v1, 8 November 2026, Bennington et al. Fetched 2026-11-13 as a 10-page PDF (182,225 bytes) from the project page https://concept.country/research/weight-space-programming; the HTML page carries the abstract but the tables are PDF-only. Pre-registered confirmation study, not a vendor launch: the subject is Qwen3.8-27B in thinking mode, all arms Q8_0 GGUF on one GB10 (Actual Computer), sampling per the model card (T=1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, 32,768-token cap), same seeds/harness across arms. Three arms: base, edit (nine rank-one additive updates to layers 32-48 even, alpha 0.1, ||dW||/||W|| ~0.5%), and a NORM-MATCHED RANDOM CONTROL (same matrices, same ||dW||, random orthogonal direction) - the control is the load-bearing comparison and it moves nothing. Table 1 confirms 86.1 vs 81.8 GPQA, 71.0 vs 58.0 LCB, 82.7 vs 79.3 IFBench, with bootstrap CIs. Section 5 discloses a measurement defect: a follow-up sampling pass appended rows into the same result files (GPQA 633/792/396 rows against 396 per arm), and three separate analysis scripts were wrong; the published numbers are the recomputed, sample-filtered ones. The paper itself reports the base BELOW Qwen's own card figures (81.8 vs 89.2 GPQA, 58.0 vs 90.3 LCB), so its deltas are within-harness only. Code/artifacts: github.com/conceptcountry/weight-space-programming, Apache-2.0.
